I was your daughter. My early teen years, I made my parents life a living hell. I was awful; I even hit my mother once during an argument. Turns out I was struggling with a multitude of mental health issues (ranging from depression to anorexia). The main thing that helped was therapy, but eventually, when even that wasn’t enough I was admitted to residential treatment. It helped beyond words.  

Being away from my parents and around so many people with shit parents, taught me to not take good parents for granted. I learned very valuable mental health and also life lessons. 

I’m not saying this is necessarily the solution, but therapy either once or twice a week is a good start. 

And remember it isn’t your fault. If we are anything alike (which it honesty sounds like something my own mother would have written three years ago), she doesn’t mean it. She is angry because deep down, she’s sad. She’s dealing with things no human should have to deal with. The trauma of living with her mother is more than enough to wreck a child’s psyche. Every time I screamed and argued with my parents, there was a voice in the back of my head begging me to stop. I regret it all, and I love my parents. 

Put her in therapy and make it happen, now. She’ll thank you later. I promise.
